newsitem.title: UK: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY TO WEAKER ON LOW DEMAND.
newsitem.headline: NWE FUEL OIL BARGES STEADY TO WEAKER ON LOW DEMAND.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges began the week steady to weak with short supplies of prompt material giving support but lower crude and swaps pushing prices in the opposite direction, traders said.

They said high sulphur barges traded at $93.50 and $94.50 fob for RMG material -- with the latter for very prompt product -- and $95 a tonne fob ARA for refinery product, the same level as trades late on Friday.
But later offers fell to $94 with buyers at $93/$93.50.
"There's still a shortage of prompt material that's why prices are high in general but prices are stable today as there are no enquiries. It is very, very quiet," one trader said.
Traders put the total moved at about 6,000 tonnes.
A second trader, agreeing that that there was a shortage of supplies, said downward pressure was coming from lower crude prices and from swaps, pegged lower at $93.25/$94 for August.

High sulphur fuel cargoes were also a little weaker, with one trader shaving $3 off his asking price for a cargo bought last week from a Scandinavian refiner, to offer the 25,000-tonne August 20 loader at $85 fob.
Low sulphur cargoes were also quiet but assessed a little weaker with swaps up to $1 lower, traders said.
